objectives: Survey the world's macro-regions + their constitutive physical + human characteristics.
Identify sub-continental regions of distinctive geographic interest.
Apply formal, functional, perceptual region typologies + Cohen + de Blij frameworks.

slides.title: World regions — twelve macro-zones
slides.body:
**Regional geography** is the synthesis that integrates physical + human geography on geographically meaningful units. Classical regional geography (Hartshorne, Vidal de la Blache, Whittlesey) gave way to quantitative + critical geography in the 20th century, then re-emerged as a synthesizing scaffold for understanding the world.

A canonical 12-realm scheme (after **Harm de Blij** + **Peter Muller** *Geography: Realms, Regions, + Concepts* + AAG world regions framework):

**1. Europe** (~750 M; 10.5 M km² incl Russian European part):
- Physical: Northern + Atlantic + Central + Mediterranean + Eastern subregions; Alps + Pyrenees + Carpathians + Urals; Gulf-Stream-warmed maritime climate west; Mediterranean Csa south.
- Human: ~50 nation-states + EU + Schengen; Indo-European Romance/Germanic/Slavic core; Christian heritage; post-WWII unification + integration; ageing population, declining native fertility; large immigration debates.
- Hubs: London, Paris, Berlin, Frankfurt, Brussels, Amsterdam, Milan, Madrid, Rome, Moscow, Istanbul.

**2. Russia** (sometimes its own realm; ~144 M; 17 M km²): largest country; spans 11 time zones; Slavic + ~190 ethnicities; petrostate + military power; post-2022 reorientation.

**3. East Asia** (~1.6 B; China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Mongolia): Sino-Tibetan + Japonic + Koreanic languages; Confucian + Buddhist + Shinto + Daoist heritage; East Asian Miracle (Japan 1950s, S Korea 1960s+, Taiwan 1970s+, China 1980s+); now ~25% of global GDP.

**4. South Asia** (~1.9 B; India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives): Indo-Gangetic Plain breadbasket; Himalaya north; monsoon-driven; Hindi-Urdu-Bengali-Tamil-Telugu-Kannada-Marathi-etc.; Hindu-Muslim-Sikh-Buddhist-Jain-Christian diversity; world's most populous region; demographic dividend window.

**5. Southeast Asia** (~680 M; ASEAN-11): mainland (Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar) + maritime (Indonesia, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Timor-Leste); Austronesian + Mon-Khmer + Tai + Tibeto-Burman; tropical monsoon; manufacturing + electronics + tourism.

**6. Middle East + North Africa (MENA)** (~600 M): Arabic + Hebrew + Persian + Turkish + Berber + Kurdish; Islamic majority with Christian + Jewish + Druze + Yazidi minorities; petroleum reserves; arid + semi-arid climates; Israel-Palestine + Iran-Saudi + Turkey + Syria + Yemen + Sudan conflicts.

**7. Sub-Saharan Africa** (~1.2 B; 49 countries): Niger-Congo + Afro-Asiatic + Nilo-Saharan + Khoisan languages; physical diversity from Sahel to rainforest to highlands to Kalahari; youngest median age (~19); fastest population growth; abundant minerals + farmland; varied governance + development outcomes; AfCFTA continental free-trade since 2021.

**8. Latin America (Middle + South America)** (~660 M): Spanish + Portuguese + Indigenous (Quechua, Aymara, Mayan, Nahuatl, Guarani); Catholic majority + evangelical growth; physical span Atacama desert → Amazon → Patagonia; resource economies; high inequality; democratization waves + recent populism debates.

**9. Oceania (Australia, NZ, Pacific Islands)** (~45 M): Anglo + Maori + Aboriginal + Melanesian + Polynesian + Micronesian; Australian arid + grassland + tropical north; small island states (Tuvalu, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Fiji, Samoa, Tonga) most exposed to sea-level rise.

**10. North America (Anglo-America)** (~370 M): US + Canada + Greenland; English (+ French in Québec); diverse physical from Arctic to subtropics; settler-colonial + immigration history; high incomes; agricultural + industrial + tech leadership.

**11. Central America + Caribbean** (often grouped with Latin America): Mexico-Panama isthmus + Caribbean islands; Spanish + English + French + Dutch + Indigenous + Creole languages; migration corridors to US; hurricane belt; remittance-dependent economies.

**12. Polar + cryospheric regions** (Arctic + Antarctic): no permanent population in Antarctica (treaty 1959); Arctic indigenous peoples (Inuit, Sámi, Nenets, Yupik); melting ice + opening shipping + resource access reshape geopolitics.

slides.title: Sub-continental regions of distinctive geographic interest
slides.body:
Within macro-regions, certain **sub-continental zones** stand out as objects of integrated physical + human geography. Twelve illustrative cases:

**Mediterranean Basin** (~500 M; 22 countries):
- Linked by sea since antiquity; Phoenician, Greek, Roman, Arab, Ottoman trade; Csa Mediterranean climate; sclerophyllous vegetation (matorral, maquis, garrigue); olive + grape + wheat triad; biodiversity hotspot; climate-change frontline (heat, drought, fire, marine heatwaves).

**Sahel** (West-Central Africa, ~1000 km wide, ~5400 km long):
- Transition between Sahara + Sudanian savanna; 200-600 mm/yr rainfall; pastoralism + millet + sorghum; Charney 1975 albedo + biogeophysical-feedback hypothesis; 1968-1985 drought; recent rainfall recovery + intermittent crises; jihadist + climate + governance entanglements (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Chad, Sudan).

**Pampas** (Argentina, Uruguay, S Brazil):
- Temperate grassland; Mollisol soils ~1-2 m thick; agricultural breadbasket — wheat, soy, maize, cattle; gauchos + estancias as cultural landscape; commodity-boom-bust economies.

**Loess Plateau** (Northern China, ~640000 km²):
- Quaternary aeolian silt up to 300 m thick; cradle of Chinese agriculture (millet + wheat); intense gullying + erosion; massive Yellow River sediment load; PRC's 'Grain for Green' afforestation (1999-) reversed erosion.

**Indo-Gangetic Plain** (~700 M; Pakistan + India + Bangladesh):
- World's most populous agricultural plain; alluvium from Himalayan rivers; Ganges + Yamuna + Brahmaputra; Green Revolution wheat + rice belt; groundwater overdraft crisis; severe air pollution; ~700 M people on ~700000 km².

**Yangtze Delta** (~150 M; Shanghai + Suzhou + Hangzhou + Nanjing):
- China's most economically productive region; ~25% of national GDP on <2% of area; tidal flats + paddy + canal landscape; coastal subsidence + sea-level threats; Yangtze + Huai water transfers (South-to-North Project).

**Ruhr Valley** (Germany, ~5 M):
- 19th-c industrial heartland — coal + steel + heavy industry; post-1970s deindustrialization + green transformation; Emscher Park IBA 1989-99 as exemplar urban-ecological renewal; lessons for global rust-belt regions.

**Pacific Rim** (Asia-Pacific coastal arc):
- Trade + GDP gravity center; world's largest seaports (Shanghai, Singapore, Ningbo, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Busan, Qingdao, HK, LA-Long Beach, Tianjin); Pacific 'Ring of Fire' tectonics (Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, US West Coast, Chile, Mexico); tsunamis (2004 Sumatra, 2011 Tōhoku) shape coastal geography.

**Silicon Valley** (San Francisco Peninsula + South Bay, ~5 M):
- Stanford + Berkeley + UC + Bay Area defense + venture capital; Hewlett-Packard 1939 garage → Fairchild 1957 → Intel 1968 → Apple 1976 → Google 1998 → OpenAI 2015 → Anthropic 2021; cluster theory exemplar; replicated imperfectly elsewhere (Shenzhen, Boston Route 128, Bangalore, Tel Aviv, Berlin); now AI hardware + foundation models.

**Greater Tokyo (Kantō Plain)** (~37 M):
- World's largest metro; Edo founded 1457, capital since 1868; major financial + manufacturing + cultural hub; trans-Pacific gravity center; megacity-scale earthquake risk; Edogawa + Sumida + Arakawa flood-control engineering.

**Mexico's Bajío + Maquiladora Border** (Querétaro + Aguascalientes + Guanajuato + Chihuahua + Tamaulipas):
- Post-NAFTA industrial corridor; aerospace + autos + electronics; US-Mexico migration + remittances; cartel violence + geopolitics; nearshoring boom.

**Mekong Region** (China-Myanmar-Laos-Thailand-Cambodia-Vietnam):
- ~70 M people; rice + fisheries + agriculture; Chinese upstream dams alter sediment + flow; Mekong River Commission; climate + dam-induced salinization in Vietnamese delta.

These sub-continental cases serve as **integrative laboratories** where physical, human, economic, + political geography converge in tractable, place-specific ways.

slides.title: Methodology — formal, functional, perceptual regions
slides.body:
**Region** is the central unit of regional geography. Three classical typologies (Whittlesey 1954; Hartshorne *The Nature of Geography* 1939; refined by de Blij):

**Formal (uniform) regions**:
- Defined by **uniformity** in one or more attributes — language, climate, soil, religion, agricultural type.
- Examples: Köppen Cfb oceanic region; Niger-Congo language area; Catholic Latin America; Mollisol-rich US Corn Belt; Mediterranean climate zone.
- Boundaries are necessarily fuzzy; transitions are real.

**Functional (nodal) regions**:
- Defined by **interaction** around a core or node — newspaper circulation area, commuting shed, milkshed, banking hinterland, port catchment, web-traffic catchment.
- Examples: NYC commuter shed; Greater Tokyo functional region; Singapore port hinterland; Shanghai's Yangtze-delta hinterland; CDC public-health regions.
- Functional regions can be modeled with gravity + Reilly's law of retail gravitation (1931) + Christaller threshold-range theory.

**Perceptual (vernacular) regions**:
- Defined by **shared perception** — 'The South' in the US, 'the Bible Belt', 'New England', 'Patagonia', 'the Outback', 'the West Bank' (cultural connotations), 'Latin America' itself.
- Studied via mental-map surveys (Lynch *The Image of the City* 1960; Gould + White *Mental Maps* 1974), focus groups, language analysis.
- **Wilbur Zelinsky** mapped US vernacular regions via newspaper + telephone-directory references in the 1980s.

**Cohen's geopolitical regions** (Saul B. Cohen):
- Geopolitical **realms** + **regions** + **shatterbelts** + **gateways**.
- A **gateway** is a region of mediation + exchange (e.g., Eastern Europe between West + Russia; Caribbean between Americas + Africa).
- The framework remains an authoritative geopolitical scaffold.

**de Blij's *Geography: Realms, Regions + Concepts***:
- **Harm de Blij (1935-2014)** — Dutch-American geographer; multiple editions of the textbook + popular books (*Why Geography Matters*, *The Power of Place*). Argued strongly for regional geography in an era of globalization; advanced UNESCO + AAG curricula.

**Modern regional geography**:
- **Critical regional geography** (Doreen Massey *Spatial Divisions of Labour* 1984) — regions as social-political constructions, products of capital + power, not pre-existing natural units.
- **Relational regions** (Allen + Massey + Cochrane 1998) — regions defined by external connections + flows, not boundaries.
- **New regional geography** (Gilbert + Massey 1980s+) — integrating critical theory with place-based synthesis.
- **Re-regionalization** post-globalization — re-emphasis on supply-chain regions, EU regions, Belt + Road sub-regions, climate-adaptation regions.

**The discipline's recurring lesson**: regions are useful as analytic + administrative units, but they are constructed + contested, never natural givens. The same territory belongs simultaneously to multiple region-systems (formal climate region, functional economic region, perceptual cultural region, political-administrative region) + the choice of which to emphasize is itself a political + intellectual act.

question.question: Define a region for studying climate-adaptation in West Africa
question.goal: Construct a region for a project on climate-adaptation in West Africa's Sahel. Choose formal + functional + perceptual elements + justify boundaries.

acceptedAnswers: Sahel formal region: 200-600 mm/yr annual precipitation belt, ~12-18°N, transition between Sahara + Sudanian savanna

hints: What climatic + ecological uniformity defines the Sahel?
steps.reveal: **Formal**: the Sahel is the 200-600 mm/yr precipitation belt, ~12-18°N, BSh climate, transition between Sahara desert + Sudanian savanna. Vegetation: thorny acacia + grass + millet-sorghum agriculture + transhumant pastoralism. Defined by climate + ecology. The 1968-1985 drought + Charney albedo hypothesis are tied to this formal boundary.

acceptedAnswers: functional regions: transhumance corridors, pastoralist-farmer interactions, market sheds of major cities (Bamako, Ouagadougou, Niamey, Maiduguri, N'Djamena), cross-border ethnic networks

steps.reveal: **Functional**: Sahelian livelihoods are organized around transhumance corridors (north-south seasonal movement of livestock 500-1500 km), millet + sorghum + cotton market sheds for Bamako-Ouagadougou-Niamey-Maiduguri-N'Djamena, cross-border Fulani-Tuareg-Hausa-Songhai-Kanuri ethnic networks, + remittance flows from coastal cities + Europe + the Gulf. Functional regions cut across colonial-era borders.

acceptedAnswers: 'Sahel' as perceived region: shared identity of dryland West African + Sahelian states (G5 Sahel, AES); evokes drought + jihadism + pastoralism + Sahelo-Saharan culture

steps.reveal: **Perceptual**: 'Sahel' carries vernacular weight — political (G5 Sahel founded 2014; Alliance of Sahel States/AES 2023 after the Mali-Burkina-Niger coups), cultural (Sahelo-Saharan music, Manding empires, Hausa polities), + media-imagined (drought, jihadism, climate-crisis trope). The perceived Sahel partially overlaps but differs from formal + functional Sahels.

steps.prompt: How would Cohen + de Blij + critical-regional approaches integrate these?

acceptedAnswers: Cohen: Sahel as a shatterbelt + gateway; de Blij: West African realm + Sahel sub-region; critical regional: Sahel as product of colonial borders, climate, capital, conflict + agency

hints: How do realm + shatterbelt + critical lens combine?
steps.reveal: **Cohen**: the Sahel is increasingly classified as a **shatterbelt** — strategically located between Maghreb + Sub-Saharan Africa + Atlantic + Sahara; fragmented states; Russian Africa Corps + French Barkhane + ECOWAS + AES rivalries. **de Blij**: Sahel as a sub-region of the Sub-Saharan African + transitional realm. **Critical regional geography (Massey, Hart)**: Sahel as historically + relationally produced — colonial borders, post-independence statecraft, droughts, agricultural commodity prices, Atlantic + Saharan trade, French + Russian + Chinese + Turkish + Gulf interventions, jihadi networks, climate change. The 'Sahel' is not a natural unit but a useful + contested scaffold for integrated geographic analysis.

question.question: Why does de Blij argue regional geography remains essential in a globalized world?
options: **Harm de Blij (1935-2014)** — author of *Geography: Realms, Regions, + Concepts* (multiple editions) + *Why Geography Matters* (2005) + *The Power of Place* (2008) — argued **against the flat-earth thesis** (Friedman 2005). His core claim: globalization has not erased place; it has redistributed it. Most humans remain locally rooted (de Blij's term: *locals* — 90%+ of humanity); only a thin layer of *globals* + *mobals* move freely. Regional geography is essential because: (1) it integrates physical + human + economic + political variables on geographically meaningful units; (2) climate change, conflict, supply-chain disruption, pandemics, migration all play out unevenly across regions; (3) place + culture + landscape + governance are sticky; (4) the failure to teach regional geography produces strategic + foreign-policy + business + climate-adaptation errors; (5) regional knowledge underpins informed citizenship in a multipolar world. de Blij combined this argument with engaging writing + UNESCO + AAG curricular activism; his textbook taught generations of US students + remains in print.
question.explanation: de Blij argued globalization redistributes rather than erases place. Most humans (locals) remain locally rooted; globals + mobals are a thin layer. Regional geography integrates physical + human variables on meaningful units; climate, conflict, supply chains, pandemics, migration play out unevenly; place + culture + governance are sticky. Failure to teach regional geography produces strategic, foreign-policy, business, + climate-adaptation errors.

hints: Why does it matter for policy?
slides.workedSolution: de Blij — globalization redistributes rather than erases place. Locals (90%+) stay rooted; globals + mobals are a thin layer. Regions integrate physical + human variables on meaningful units; climate, conflict, supply chains play out unevenly. Failure to teach regional geography produces strategic, foreign-policy, business, + adaptation errors. *Why Geography Matters* (2005) + textbooks remain standard.

question.question: Drafting a regional-strategy chapter for a country profile
question.prompt: An international development bank asks you to draft the regional-geography chapter of its country profile on **Vietnam**. Apply de Blij + Cohen + critical regional geography: (1) **Macro-realm + region** — Vietnam in Southeast Asia + within the mainland (Indochinese) sub-region; physical (Annamite Cordillera, Red River + Mekong deltas, Truong Son range, ~3260 km coast) + human (Kinh majority + 53 ethnic minorities; Vietnamese language; Mahayana Buddhist + Catholic + Hòa Hảo + Cao Đài; communist single-party state). (2) **Formal regions within Vietnam** — North (Red River delta), North Central, South Central, Central Highlands, South (Mekong delta). (3) **Functional regions** — Hanoi-Haiphong corridor; HCMC-Bien Hoa-Vung Tau; manufacturing zones; ports; agricultural sheds. (4) **Perceptual regions** — North-Center-South cultural identities; Tonkin/Annam/Cochinchine colonial echoes. (5) **Cohen geopolitical framing** — Vietnam in South China Sea shatterbelt; gateway between China + ASEAN. (6) **Mekong Region** — upstream Chinese + Laotian dams + delta sea-level + salinity threats; Mekong River Commission. (7) **Critical regional analysis** — French colonial + Vietnam War + Đổi mới reform legacies; FDI + GVC integration (Apple supplier shift from China to Vietnam); migration to coastal cities; climate-vulnerable delta. (8) **Climate-adaptation regional strategy** — Mekong + Red River deltas, coastal cities (HCMC, Da Nang), highlands. Deliver an 8-page chapter integrating physical + human + economic + political + critical-regional perspectives.

question.question: The Indo-Gangetic Plain supports ~700 M people on ~700000 km². Compute the population density (people / km², to nearest 10).
question.hint: Density = 700 × 10⁶ / 700000 = 1000 people/km². One of the densest agricultural macro-regions on Earth — alluvial Mollisol-ish + monsoon-driven; Green Revolution + groundwater overdraft + air-pollution challenges.

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, integrate world-region + sub-continental + methodological regional geography by naming at least eight regions + three methodologies + one figure.
question.rubric: Mentions: world regions — Europe, Russia, East Asia, South Asia, SE Asia, Middle East + North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Oceania, North America, Polar; sub-continental — Mediterranean Basin, Sahel, Pampas, Loess Plateau, Indo-Gangetic Plain, Yangtze Delta, Ruhr, Pacific Rim, Silicon Valley, Greater Tokyo, Mekong; methodologies — formal/functional/perceptual (Whittlesey), Cohen geopolitical realms + shatterbelts + gateways, de Blij realms, critical/relational (Massey, Hart). Figure: **de Blij** + *Why Geography Matters* + Realms, Regions + Concepts arguing regional geography remains essential despite globalization. Concludes: regions are constructed + contested, never natural; the same territory belongs to multiple region-systems; integrating physical + human + economic + political + critical perspectives is the discipline's core value.
